audit.scope: full static review of source, configuration, dependencies and supply chain
audit.verdict: NOT PRODUCTION READY - multiple pre-authentication remote code execution, SQL injection and path traversal vulnerabilities

findings.title: Arbitrary file read via path traversal
findings.summary: The 'file' and 'path' query parameters are joined to the 'documents' base directory with path.join(), which normalizes '..' segments. No traversal check, no authentication.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated read of arbitrary server files (/etc/passwd, .env, process env) and arbitrary directory listing. All customer invoice PDFs under documents/invoices are exposed.
findings.remediation: Use path.resolve() + verify the resolved path starts with baseDir + sep; apply an allowlist of extensions and subdirectories.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in product search
findings.summary: The 'q' parameter is interpolated into a LIKE clause and executed with prisma.$queryRawUnsafe. The zod schema only constrains it to z.string().
findings.impact: Full database read including the users table (emails, password hashes, roles) and all support/password-reset tokens; data modification.
findings.remediation: Replace with Prisma ORM findMany using contains filters, or use parameterized prisma.$queryRaw tagged templates.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in tracking endpoint
findings.summary: The IP is taken from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement. userAgent and path are escaped, ip is not.
findings.impact: Pre-auth SQL injection on every page view. UNION extraction of the users table, log table poisoning, data modification.
findings.remediation: Use prisma.visitorLog.create(); derive the IP from a trusted proxy only.

findings.title: Privilege escalation via signup role parameter
findings.summary: signupBodySchema explicitly accepts an optional 'role' field and the route writes it to the database. The schema also uses .passthrough(), allowing additional User fields.
findings.impact: Self-registration as ADMIN. Complete administrative takeover with no credential required.
findings.remediation: Remove 'role' from the schema, use .strict(), and hardcode role: 'CUSTOMER' on creation.

findings.title: Account takeover via support-access token for arbitrary email
findings.summary: POST accepts an 'email' body field and issues a support access token for ANY user, including admins. The token is then exchangeable for a full session carrying the target's role.
findings.impact: Any authenticated normal user becomes ADMIN. Tokens are valid for 365 days and revoked is not checked at redemption time.
findings.remediation: Always use user.email; never accept a target email from the body. Check supportToken.revoked. Shorten expiry to hours and notify the affected account.

findings.title: XXE in supplier order XML import
findings.summary: libxmljs.parseXmlString is called with noent: true (expands entities) and dtdload: true (loads external DTDs).
findings.impact: Local file disclosure via file:// entities, SSRF via http:// entities (including cloud metadata endpoints), Billion Laughs memory exhaustion DoS.
findings.remediation: Set noent: false, dtdload: false, nonet: true. Validate against an XSD, limit body size and set a parse timeout.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SSRF in support ticket submission
findings.summary: The user-supplied screenshotUrl is fetched server-side with no destination validation, no timeout, no size limit, and with an X-Internal-Request header attached. The response body is returned to the caller.
findings.impact: SSRF to internal services and cloud metadata; chains into the /internal header-based auth bypass (QB-021); content is reflected as HTML enabling XSS (QB-018).
findings.remediation: Allowlist https hosts, resolve DNS and reject private/loopback/link-local ranges, follow redirects manually with per-hop validation, set AbortSignal.timeout and a response size cap, drop the internal header, require auth.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5
findings.summary: hashMD5() uses crypto.createHash('md5') with no salt and no work factor.
findings.impact: Hashes are recovered in seconds with commodity GPUs and are vulnerable to rainbow tables; identical passwords share identical hashes across accounts.
findings.remediation: Migrate to Argon2id (argon2 npm) or bcrypt cost 12+ / scrypt. Force password reset for all MD5 accounts.

findings.title: Plaintext passwords written to application logs
findings.summary: The login route logs the plaintext password both as a structured field and inside the log message template.
findings.impact: Every credential ever used is persisted in logs/app.log, which is readable through the SIEM panel whose credentials are hardcoded (QB-011) and is mounted as a Docker volume.
findings.remediation: Remove the password from the log payload and message. Add a pino secret redactor. Rotate all exposed credentials.

findings.title: JWT signing secret defaults to the literal string 'secret'
findings.summary: const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'secret'. Verified: JWT_SECRET is not set anywhere in the repository, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, or setup.sh, so every default deployment signs tokens with 'secret'.
findings.impact: Anyone can forge an authToken cookie with role ADMIN and gain full administrative access without any credential.
findings.remediation: Remove the fallback and throw at startup if JWT_SECRET is missing. Generate a random >=32 byte secret per deployment and rotate all issued tokens.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in source code

locations.value: SIEM root/admin credentials + unsigned siem_session cookie compared to the literal 'authenticated'
seeded admin account with a trivial password

findings.summary: Six distinct secrets are hardcoded. The SIEM session cookie is not signed at all, so 'Cookie: siem_session=authenticated' bypasses SIEM authentication entirely.
findings.impact: Access to the application logs (which contain plaintext passwords), forgeable share tokens exposing any order, access to the restricted MCP tool, and a known admin account.
findings.remediation: Move all credentials to required environment variables that fail fast; sign session cookies with HMAC; remove the diag endpoint or protect it with a rotatable secret; randomize the seeded admin password.

findings.title: Secrets committed to the repository and baked into the Docker image
findings.summary: .env.local holds a payment secret and a flag token. .gitignore lists .env but not .env.local; .dockerignore lists .env but not .env.local, and the Dockerfile does 'COPY . .'.
findings.impact: The secret is versionable and is embedded in the shipped image layer, retrievable via docker save / docker history / registry pull. NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefixed values are additionally inlined into the browser bundle.
findings.remediation: Add .env* / .env*.local to both ignore files, git rm --cached the file, purge history, rotate all values, and stop using NEXT_PUBLIC_ for sensitive material.

findings.title: Next.js 15.2.2 and zod carry critical known vulnerabilities
findings.summary: npm audit reports 33 vulnerabilities: 2 critical, 13 high, 16 moderate, 2 low. next 15.2.2 has two unauthenticated RCEs in the image optimization API (SVG and AVIF), an RCE in the React Flight protocol, a critical middleware authorization bypass, and a middleware bypass via segment-prefetch routes. zod < 4.6.6 allows memory exhaustion when validating oversized constrained collections (directly applicable, as every endpoint validates with zod).
findings.remediation: Upgrade to next >= 15.5.29 and zod >= 4.6.6, pin with overrides, and enforce npm audit --audit-level=high in CI.

findings.title: Predictable password reset token
findings.summary: The reset token is MD5(email + unix_seconds) with a one hour expiry.
findings.impact: The token can be forged for any victim with at most 3600 guesses, since the email is public and the timestamp window is bounded. Leads to arbitrary account password reset.
findings.remediation: Use crypto.randomBytes(32) opaque tokens, store only their SHA-256 hash, shorten expiry to 15-60 minutes, invalidate on first use.

findings.title: Unsigned SIEM session cookie
findings.summary: Authentication succeeds when the siem_session cookie equals the literal string 'authenticated', with no signature, no expiry check and no server-side state.
findings.impact: Full authentication bypass for the log viewer, which exposes the plaintext credentials logged by QB-009.
findings.remediation: Remove the cookie check or sign the value with an HMAC including an exp claim; prefer reusing withAuth/withAdminAuth.

findings.title: IDOR on the order detail endpoint
findings.summary: prisma.order.findUnique({ where: { id } }) does not filter by the authenticated user. Sequential IDs (ORD-001, ORD-002) make enumeration trivial.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can read any other customer's order: total, status, email, full delivery address. The sibling route /api/orders/[id]/share correctly filters by userId, confirming this is an omission.
findings.remediation: Use findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } }) and allow an ADMIN override explicitly. Apply the same check to the wishlist GET.

findings.title: Stored XSS in the admin analytics panel
findings.summary: visit.ip is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The value originates from the attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and is persisted in visitor_logs.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated attacker stores a script payload that executes in every admin browser viewing analytics, enabling session theft and full store takeover.
findings.remediation: Remove dangerouslySetInnerHTML and render {visit.ip} as text. Validate the IP format server-side before persisting.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via remote screenshot content in the support form
findings.summary: screenshotContent, fetched server-side from a user-supplied URL, is injected as raw HTML.
findings.impact: Attacker-hosted HTML executes in the browser. Combined with QB-007 this turns the SSRF into a same-origin XSS vector.
findings.remediation: Render as plain text or sanitize with DOMPurify on the server. Never inject remote content as HTML.

findings.title: SQL injection in the admin reviews audit
findings.summary: The 'author' query parameter is interpolated into SQL executed through better-sqlite3 db.exec and db.prepare.
findings.impact: ADMIN-gated, but the attacker is admin in practice via QB-004/QB-005. Full database read including user password hashes.
findings.remediation: Use Prisma filters or parameterized prepared statements (db.prepare(sql).all(authorFilter)).

findings.title: SQL injection in the order search endpoint
findings.summary: The 'status' body field is interpolated into a WHERE clause executed with prisma.$queryRawUnsafe. user.id is interpolated as well.
findings.impact: Database read and modification by any authenticated user; user.id becomes a second injection vector once tokens can be forged (QB-010).
findings.remediation: Parameterize with prisma.$queryRaw tagged templates or resolve via the ORM.

findings.title: Header-based authentication bypass on the internal dashboard
findings.summary: Access is granted purely on the presence of the x-internal-request: true request header, which any client can set.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated access to the internal dashboard. Chains with QB-007 because the SSRF attaches that same header.
findings.remediation: Replace with real session and role checks, or remove the page.

findings.title: Stored XSS via SVG product image upload
findings.summary: image/svg+xml is an accepted upload type and the file is served publicly from the same origin with that content type.
findings.impact: Same-origin stored XSS; script execution in any visitor's session, including admins.
findings.remediation: Remove SVG from the allowlist, or serve it with Content-Disposition: attachment and CSP: sandbox. Validate magic bytes rather than the declared Content-Type.

findings.title: User export exposes password hashes and internal diagnostics
findings.summary: ALLOWED_USER_FIELDS includes 'password'. Error responses embed getSystemDiagnostics() with the Node version, database status and full stack traces.
findings.impact: Password hash export and server internals disclosure to any authenticated user.
findings.remediation: Remove 'password' from the allowlist; never return stack traces or diagnostics to the client.

findings.title: Live stream hijack by any authenticated user
findings.summary: A non-admin can set liveVideoId. The code computes a 'hijacked' flag but still persists the change and returns ok: true.
findings.impact: Denial of service on the official broadcast and brand-phishing via attacker content embedded in the official site.
findings.remediation: Reject with 403 and do not persist; audit the attempt.

findings.title: Order total is attacker controlled
findings.summary: The 'total' body field is persisted verbatim. Coupon discounting is computed client-side in /api/coupon/apply and never re-applied server-side. The X-Payment-Auth header carrying NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMENT_SECRET is never validated.
findings.impact: Orders can be created for an arbitrary amount (e.g. 0.01), causing direct financial loss.
findings.remediation: Compute the total server-side from cart contents and coupon; validate coupons at charge time; never trust a client-supplied total.

findings.title: Predictable gift card codes
findings.summary: Codes are produced by a hand-rolled LCG seeded with createdAt.getTime(), giving a 32-bit seed space.
findings.impact: Codes can be enumerated by brute-forcing the timestamp seed, allowing forgery and redemption of other users' gift cards for unearned credit.
findings.remediation: Use crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('base64url') for ~60 bits of entropy.

findings.title: Middleware decodes the JWT without verifying its signature
findings.summary: decodeJWT base64-decodes the payload and checks only exp. The ADMIN role decision is made on entirely unauthenticated data.
findings.impact: Any base64 payload with role ADMIN passes the middleware check. Today it guards one route, but it establishes an authorization pattern based on unverified data.
findings.remediation: Verify the HMAC signature with timingSafeEqual, or remove authorization logic from the middleware and rely on withAuth/withAdminAuth.

findings.title: Unbounded write amplification in the tracking endpoint
findings.summary: Each request inserts a row into visitor_logs with no auth, no rate limit and no body size cap.
findings.impact: Database growth and analytics degradation; DoS of the admin panel.
findings.remediation: Rate limit per IP, cap the body size, and sample or aggregate in memory.

findings.title: Secondary SSRF and unauthenticated AI proxy
findings.summary: The client supplies both apiKey and mcpServerUrl. The server calls the Mistral API with the caller's key and performs tools/list and tools/call against an arbitrary URL.
findings.impact: Second SSRF surface able to send JSON-RPC to internal services, including the app's own MCP endpoint with the internal session header; the endpoint also acts as an unauthenticated proxy to a paid third-party API.
findings.remediation: Remove mcpServerUrl from the public API, allowlist MCP hosts, use a server-side MISTRAL_API_KEY, and rate limit.

findings.title: Prompt injection filter is trivially bypassed
findings.summary: Four regexes guard the user message, but tool output is never filtered and the tool-calling loop is unconstrained. The system prompt embeds an internal validation code and instructs the model to echo reference codes from tool responses.
findings.impact: Extraction of internal tool data and the embedded code via ordinary language paraphrases.
findings.remediation: Enforce authorization inside each tool rather than trusting a shared hasSession boolean; keep secrets out of prompts.

findings.title: Session cookie lacks hardening
findings.summary: authToken is set with httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure only in production, a 7 day maxAge and no __Host- prefix.
findings.impact: Without the __Host- prefix a compromised sibling subdomain can overwrite the session cookie (cookie tossing); the long lifetime widens the window for token theft.
findings.remediation: Set secure unconditionally, use the __Host- prefix, reduce maxAge to 1-4 hours with sliding refresh.

findings.title: No rate limiting and user enumeration on auth routes
findings.summary: No rate limiting anywhere. Signup answers 'Email already registered' while login answers 'Invalid credentials', enabling account enumeration. forgot-password deletes all existing tokens for the email, invalidating other sessions.
findings.impact: Credential brute forcing (worsened by MD5 hashes), account enumeration, reset-email flooding, denial of service on password reset.
findings.remediation: Add per-IP and per-account rate limiting with exponential backoff, unify error messages, and avoid destructive token deletion.

findings.title: Reviews can be posted unauthenticated with a spoofed author
findings.summary: The POST handler does not use withAuth; getAuthenticatedUser is optional and a client-supplied author value takes precedence.
findings.impact: Anonymous spam and impersonation of arbitrary users, enabling phishing content on the storefront.
findings.remediation: Require authentication and derive the author from the session.

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.summary: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, frame-ancestors or Permissions-Policy are configured.
findings.impact: Removes the defence-in-depth that would otherwise contain the XSS findings QB-017, QB-018 and QB-022.
findings.remediation: Add a headers() function with a restrictive CSP and the standard hardening headers.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.summary: The Dockerfile has no USER directive, so the application process runs as root.
findings.impact: Combined with QB-001 and any code execution, the blast radius extends to the host or sibling containers.
findings.remediation: Create an unprivileged user, switch to it before CMD, and tighten volume permissions.

findings.title: Internal paths and exception details leaked in responses
findings.summary: Responses expose SUPPLIER_REGISTRY_PATH, the raw libxmljs error message (which can contain file contents) and Prisma stack traces.
findings.impact: Information disclosure of internal layout and data via error channels.
findings.remediation: Log details server-side with a request id and return a generic message.

findings.title: Upload validation relies on a client-declared content type and a path blacklist
findings.summary: The upload route trusts file.type from the client and never inspects the actual bytes. The static file server blocks '..' with a string check instead of verifying the resolved path stays under the uploads directory.
findings.impact: Type confusion and content-type bypass; fragile path protection.
findings.remediation: Validate magic bytes, allowlist extensions, and use resolve() plus a directory prefix check.

findings.title: Support session tokens live a year and ignore the revoked flag
findings.summary: The revoked field is never checked at redemption and the issued JWT expires in 365 days.
findings.impact: Revoking a token in the database does not invalidate an already-issued session.
findings.remediation: Check revoked, shorten the expiry, and support session revocation via a jti denylist.

findings.title: Prisma Studio launched unauthenticated by the setup script
findings.summary: npx prisma studio -b none is started in the background, exposing the whole database on port 5555 without authentication.
findings.impact: Full unauthenticated database read/write if the port is reachable or forwarded.
findings.remediation: Remove it from the setup script and bind it to 127.0.0.1 when used manually.

findings.title: Coupon redemption race condition
findings.summary: usedCount is incremented non-atomically and the discount is never applied to the persisted total.
findings.impact: Coupons can be used beyond maxUses under concurrency; discount accounting is inconsistent.
findings.remediation: Use updateMany with a usedCount < maxUses condition inside a transaction and apply the discount server-side.

findings.title: Order ID generation is racy and O(n)
findings.summary: The next ORD-nnn id is computed by scanning every existing order and retrying on conflict.
findings.impact: Duplicate id collisions under concurrency, performance degradation as the table grows.
findings.remediation: Use a database sequence or a UUID.

findings.title: Gift card redemption loads all pending cards
findings.summary: All PENDING gift cards are fetched into memory and compared one by one in a constant-time loop.
findings.impact: Memory pressure and latency growth as the gift card table grows; the constant-time comparison does not address the predictability of QB-026.
findings.remediation: Look up the card by a hash of the code and compare with timingSafeEqual.

findings.title: Floating point used for monetary values
findings.summary: Product.price, Order.total, GiftCard.amount and User.creditBalance are all Float.
findings.impact: Rounding errors accumulate across totals and balances.
findings.remediation: Use Prisma Decimal and handle currency as integer minor units.

findings.title: Response filtering strips any value containing the flag prefix
findings.summary: Three endpoints drop any row value whose lowercased form contains the CTF flag prefix. The two conditions are byte-identical, so one is dead code.
findings.impact: This is an anti-tamper mechanism for the CTF exercise, not a security control. In production it would be misleading obfuscation that masks rather than prevents disclosure.
findings.remediation: Remove the filter and fix the underlying exposure.

findings.title: Technology fingerprinting enabled by default
findings.summary: poweredByHeader is not disabled, so responses advertise X-Powered-By: Next.js.
findings.impact: Unnecessary technology disclosure that assists reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Set poweredByHeader: false.

findings.title: Log viewer reads the entire log file into memory
findings.summary: The full log file is read with readFileSync and split into lines on every request.
findings.impact: Memory exhaustion and latency spikes once the log file grows, especially combined with QB-009 (which stores a row per login attempt) and QB-028.
findings.remediation: Stream and paginate, or use a rotating log with an index.

attack_chains.name: Anonymous to administrator
steps: POST /api/auth/signup with role=ADMIN (QB-004) OR create a support token for admin@quokka.store and redeem it (QB-005)
Use the admin session to read the database via /api/products/search?q=' UNION SELECT... (QB-002)
Exfiltrate password hashes and impersonate any user

attack_chains.name: Anonymous to database read, no credentials at all
steps: GET /api/products/search?q=<union payload> (QB-002) or POST /api/tracking with a crafted X-Forwarded-For (QB-003)
Read users, orders, addresses, support_access_tokens and password_reset_tokens
Use the reset token (or MD5 crack, QB-008) to take over accounts (QB-014)

attack_chains.name: SSRF to internal dashboard and XSS
steps: The server attaches X-Internal-Request: true, bypassing the internal page check (QB-021)
The response content is rendered as raw HTML in the support form (QB-018)

attack_chains.name: Stored XSS to admin session theft
steps: An admin opens /admin/analytics, the payload executes in their session
The admin session yields full control of the store

attack_chains.name: Log viewer to full credential disclosure
steps: The log file contains plaintext passwords from every login attempt (QB-009)
